problem: Readers disagreed about whether a failed promise suffices; the broad appearance/reversal wording concealed different mechanisms.
discussion: Reader A defended the appearance-to-reversal reading of the launch delay.
Reader B compared the delay with hidden test results and asked where concealment and discovery occurred.
The pair retained the more demanding concealment-revelation relation and added explicit author-stance and uncertainty guidance; they did not merge all negative events to improve agreement.
decision: Clarify the interpretive claim, record the counterexample, and preserve the original disagreement. The launch delay becomes a defended negative in v0.2.
sequence: F2 collective revision and codebook freeze
F3 new v0.2 readings and collective decisions
F4 frozen simulated judgments and evaluation
holdout_policy: No holdout text or evaluation outcome was used to develop the codebook in this designed teaching chronology. All records are invented, so this is not evidence of actual prospective blinding.
